To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cochlear implant users with residual hearing in the contralateral ear are able to match the pitch of acoustic and electrical stimuli.

1) pitch comparisons of acoustical and electrically evoced sensations are possible, 2) pitch matches are influenced by the frequency of the acoustical and the electrical stimuli and by the position of stimulation in the scala tymnani, 3) pitch matches are also influenced by the pulse rate of the electrical stimulus.
the pitch of electric stimuli depends upon electrode position and pulse-rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pitch perception of cochlear implant users.
the development of a new generation of auditory brainstem implants for the treatment of deafness.
the pitch of electrical stimuli delivered by cochlear implants, and with the relationship between the pitch of electrical and acoustic stimuli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electrode position and pulse rates influence the perceived pitch of electric stimuli.
the pitch of the electrical stimulus is determined by both the pulse rate and the electrode position in a complex and nonlinear manner.
the pitch sensation of an electrical stimulus is a function of the electrode position and pulse repetition rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

pitch comparisons between electric and acoustic sensations were obtained over a large frequency range, and that the electrode position and pulse rates that matched acoustic and electric sensations varied widely between listeners.
the pitch sensations produced in cochlear implants are influenced by both pulse rate and electrode position in the cochlea.
the perceived pitch of electrical stimuli is a function of both electrode position and electric pulse rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pitch of electric stimuli can be matched with acoustic tones over a wide range in the frequency domain.
pitch is a complex percept that can be influenced by many parameters.
the electrode positions that'match' pure tones are more apical than predicted from the frequency-place map.
